study: Zhang et al. Clinical value of metagenomic next-generation sequencing by Illumina and Nanopore for the detection of pathogens in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in suspected community-acquired pneumonia patients. DOI:10.3389/fcimb.2022.1021320; corrigendum DOI:10.3389/fcimb.2024.1468511; PRJCA027972/OMIX006862
public_record_n_definition: Official OMIX display labels the ZIP Number/Samples=138 but does not define it. ZIP central-directory inspection instead found 90 mNGS FASTA and 66 ONT FASTA members; it must not be interpreted as a subject count.
other_record_n_definition: Eight manifest/list members; not biological records.
infection_adjudication_definition: Five categories (established, excluded, suspected, unknown causes, other non-infectious factors); chief physician in conjunction with other tests; information flow to/from mNGS is not publicly specified.
major_blockers: No documented deterministic subject/BALF crosswalk for all Illumina and Nanopore records; eight lexical laboratory-stem matches after an undocumented suffix transformation are not valid pairings.
The portal's 138 Number/Samples is undefined and conflicts with the 156 FASTA members in the released ZIP.
The clinical etiological-adjudication information flow is insufficient to rule out incorporation bias for an ecology outcome.
Released Illumina content is host-depleted FASTA rather than native raw reads, preventing a frozen native-Kraken2 layer.
overall_verdict: METHODS_ONLY_PARK: retain only as a diagnostic-platform reserve; do not request bulk data or use as a cross-cohort biological ecology cohort without a documented subject/specimen/platform bridge and independent clinical labels.
